rules: Team-level literature is convergent/contextual evidence, not individual ground truth.
Volume metrics are not signed automatically.
Efficiency semantics may support a direction only when the event definition itself is directional.
Role-specific or opportunity-driven metrics remain context-dependent unless stronger evidence exists.
No direction status implies a weight, threshold, percentile or score contribution.

literature.title: How to be Successful in Football: A Systematic Review
literature.use: Supports relevance of efficiency, shots and pass accuracy while emphasizing contextual variables.

literature.title: A systematic review about the performance indicators related to ball possession
literature.use: Supports strong context dependence of possession-related technical indicators and playing style.

literature.title: The Use of Match Statistics that Discriminate Between Successful and Unsuccessful Soccer Teams
literature.use: Supports attacking effectiveness and shots as discriminating indicators, without authorizing individual volume signs.

literature.title: Match success in football: insights from raw and possession-normalized key performance indicators in the Turkish professional league
literature.use: Supports offensive efficiency and negative association of cards with success while showing context/normalization effects.

literature.title: Consequences of players' dismissal in professional soccer: a crisis-related analysis of group-size effects
literature.use: Supports negative direction of red-card dismissal.

features.reason: Pass accuracy is relevant to success, but individual completion rate depends on pass difficulty, role and playing style.
Completion is an efficiency measure but long-ball difficulty and tactical purpose vary by role and style.
Cross efficiency can be useful, but literature shows context-sensitive and sometimes inconsistent effects.
At fixed attempts, a larger share of successful dribbles represents more successful 1v1 outcomes; role context is still retained.
At fixed tackle attempts, a larger success share represents more successful defensive outcomes; opportunity and role remain contextual.
Higher conversion means more goals for a given number of shots and aligns with literature emphasizing efficiency.
A blocked-shot share can reflect shot selection, defensive pressure and tactical context; no universal individual sign is approved.
Pass volume reflects involvement and style but is not universally better when higher.
An assist directly contributes to a goal under the approved event definition.
Long-ball volume is role/style dependent and cannot be globally signed.
Cross volume is opportunity and tactical-style dependent; higher volume is not universally better.
Dribble volume reflects role and attacking style rather than universal performance quality.
A turnover is an approved possession-loss event; more losses represent a direct cost, subject to later contextual weighting.
Being dispossessed is a direct possession-loss event; more occurrences represent a direct cost, subject to later contextual weighting.
Shot volume is associated with attacking success at team level but individual volume depends on role, opportunity and shot quality.
A goal directly changes match score and is intrinsically positive attacking output.
Tackle volume depends strongly on defensive role, possession state and opportunity.
Interceptions are useful defensive actions but volume is opportunity/style dependent; no universal per90 sign is approved.
Blocked-pass volume depends on defensive exposure, role and team structure.
Clearance volume may indicate successful defending or sustained defensive pressure; higher is not universally better.
Fouls are costs in some contexts but recent team-level evidence shows mixed associations; tactical fouling prevents a universal sign.
Being fouled may proxy attacking involvement but depends on role, location and game state.
Yellow cards are disciplinary sanctions and recent multiseason evidence reports a negative association with match success.
Dismissal directly reduces team playing resources and is consistently detrimental.
Conceding a penalty directly grants the opponent a high-value scoring opportunity.
Winning a penalty directly creates a high-value scoring opportunity for the player's team.
Save volume is driven by shots faced and team defensive exposure; higher volume is not universally better goalkeeper performance.
Conceded goals are undesirable outcomes but are strongly influenced by shot quality faced and team defence; no unadjusted individual sign is approved.
